users.access_save_failed: The targets could not be saved.
users.subtitle: Manage user accounts, RBAC roles and permissions.
users.title: User Management
users.error_load: Could not load the account list.
users.initial_password_hint: At least 12 characters. Shown because you have to pass it on: it stands in for a one-time pass, and the account will have to change it at first sign-in.
users.reset_hint: The account will have to change it at its next sign-in.
users.delete_consequence: and its sessions will be deleted. This is permanent.

git_tokens.title: HTTPS tokens
git_tokens.subtitle: Access tokens repositories clone with over HTTPS. Each is bound to one host and is sent to no other.
git_tokens.name: Name
git_tokens.host_hint: The bare host name, as in the repository URL: gitlab.example.com — no scheme, port or path. The token is only ever sent to this host.
git_tokens.username_hint: Some providers expect a particular username with a token (Bitbucket, some GitLab setups). Left empty, the provider default is used.
git_tokens.token_hint: A read-only token is enough to clone. It is stored encrypted and never shown again.
git_tokens.delete_confirm: will be deleted. A token still used by a repository cannot be deleted: detach it from those repositories first.
git_tokens.error_load: Could not load the HTTPS tokens.

encryption_status.current_hint: Encrypted with the current encryption key.
encryption_status.previous_key_hint: Encrypted with a previous encryption key. Add it again to move it under ENCRYPTION_KEY, then delete this one.
encryption_status.unreadable_hint: No configured key decrypts this token: the next clone that needs it will fail. Add the previous key to VECTISPIRE_PREVIOUS_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, or replace this token.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.subtitle: Your own analysers, packaged as container images and run during a scan beside Vectispire's scanners. Every account can read the registry; only the platform governor registers, changes or disables a plugin.
plugins.network_none: None — the container runs with the network cut.
plugins.no_delete: A plugin cannot be deleted, and its id never changes: the id is part of every issue it opened. Disable it to stop it everywhere; its activations are kept.
plugins.projects_none: No project. A plugin runs on nothing until a security lead switches it on for a project.
plugins.projects_hint: Switch it on or off from Solutions & projects.
plugins.id_permanent: The id can never be renamed or reused: it enters the fingerprint of every issue this plugin opens. 2 to 40 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens.
plugins.image_hint: Pinned by digest: repository@sha256: followed by 64 hex characters. A tag, even beside the digest, is refused.
plugins.languages_hint: The plugin runs only on a repository where one of these languages is present; elsewhere its step reads “not applicable”, which is not a failure.
plugins.arguments_hint: Handed to the image's entrypoint as a list, with no shell. {source} becomes /repo/source, {output} becomes /repo/output/ followed by the report file.
plugins.exit_codes_hint: Any other exit code fails the plugin's step and leaves its issues as they were. Exit 0 with an empty report means “analysed, found nothing”, and resolves every issue it opened on the repository.
plugins.network_hint: Off unless it genuinely must reach something, such as an internal rule mirror. The justification is recorded in the audit log.
plugins.signer_hint: Who must have signed the image, checked with cosign before it is pulled; an image it does not verify never runs. Keyless: the certificate identity and its OIDC issuer, both matched exactly. Or a public key. All empty: the image is trusted by its digest alone, which an executor may refuse.
plugins.signer_none: None — trusted by its digest alone.
plugins.error_load: Could not load the plugin registry.
plugins.error_exit_codes: The exit codes must be whole numbers separated by commas.
plugins.error_save: The plugin could not be saved.
plugins.error_enable: The plugin's state could not be changed.
plugins.registered_notice: {{id}} registered, manifest {{digest}}. It runs nowhere until it is switched on for a project.
plugins.updated_notice: {{id}} updated, manifest {{digest}}. Its issues and their triage are kept.
plugins.enabled_notice: {{id}} enabled: it runs from the next scan wherever it is switched on.
plugins.disabled_notice: {{id}} disabled: it runs nowhere from the next scan; its activations are kept.

sarif_imports.explain: Reports deposited by a declared internal source, with its integration key. Uploads come from CI; nothing is uploaded from here. Each row is the dated evidence of the imported issues it opened.
sarif_imports.none: No SARIF report was imported into this repository.
sarif_imports.not_visible: This repository does not exist or is not visible to you.
sarif_imports.error_load: Could not load the SARIF imports.

sarif_sources.title: Declared sources
sarif_sources.subtitle: The internal tools allowed to deposit reports for a repository — SARIF into its backlog, coverage and test reports as figures a checklist reads. An on-premise SonarQube, your own CI; never a hosted service outside the organisation. Only the platform governor declares one.
sarif_sources.upload_hint: A source uploads with its key — SARIF to POST /api/v1/repositories/{id}/sarif-imports, coverage to …/coverage-imports, test reports to …/test-report-imports; a session cannot import.
sarif_sources.internal_only: Declare only a producer inside the organisation, which already has the code. For SARIF, the tool list is compared with each run's tool.driver.name: a report from any other tool is refused.
sarif_sources.slug_hint: Part of every imported issue's identity: name the producer, not the key. Declaring the same slug again with a new key continues the same backlog.
sarif_sources.key_placeholder: Choose a key holding the scopes the chosen kinds need
sarif_sources.key_hint: One key, one source: the key names the source when it uploads.
sarif_sources.no_key: No usable key holds the scopes the chosen kinds need — sarif_import for SARIF, report_import for coverage and test reports. Issue one on the API keys screen, from an account that can act.
sarif_sources.scope_hint: Exactly one scope — a project or a repository, never the whole estate.
sarif_sources.tools_hint: Separated by commas, compared without regard to case.
sarif_sources.remove_consequence: {{slug}} will no longer be able to import. What it imported stays — issues, coverage and test reports — and keeps {{slug}} as its source.
sarif_sources.error_load: Could not load the declared sources.
sarif_sources.error_declare: The source could not be declared.
sarif_sources.error_change: The source could not be changed.
sarif_sources.kinds_hint: SARIF needs a key holding sarif_import and the tools it may deliver; coverage and test reports need report_import, and are figures a checklist reads, never findings.
sarif_sources.no_kind: Choose at least one kind of report.

report_imports.explain: Deposited by a declared internal source with its integration key, from CI; nothing is uploaded from here. These are figures a checklist reads: they open no issue and reach no gate.
report_imports.stated: Commit and branch are what the pipeline stated; nothing verifies them.
report_imports.no_coverage: No coverage report was imported for this repository.
report_imports.no_tests: No test report was imported for this repository.

checklist_templates.title: Checklist templates
checklist_templates.subtitle: Your organisation's security checklists, imported from its own workbooks. A workbook becomes a draft; its layout and answer words are confirmed on the sheet itself, its lines paired with the previous version, and only then is it published for projects to answer.
checklist_templates.error_load: Could not load the checklist templates.
checklist_templates.import_explain: The .xlsx is sent as it is and becomes the template's next version, as a draft: nothing is published in one step. A template has at most one draft at a time.
checklist_templates.slug_new_hint: A new slug creates the template: 1 to 64 lowercase letters, digits and inner hyphens.
checklist_templates.slug_existing_hint: This template exists: the workbook becomes its next version.
checklist_templates.file_hint: At most 10 MB. Macro-enabled workbooks (.xlsm) and the binary format are refused.
checklist_templates.too_large: The request body is larger than the {{limit}} bytes this route accepts.
checklist_templates.imported_notice: Version {{ordinal}} of "{{slug}}" imported as a draft. Confirm its layout below.
checklist_templates.column_header_row: Column header row found by the reader: {{row}}
checklist_templates.grid_legend: Blue: the item rows of the columns the layout names. Amber: the header cells. A column head names the field it holds; ƒ marks a formula.
checklist_templates.cells_truncated: The sheet has more cells than the preview shows: only the first 20,000 are drawn.
checklist_templates.layout_proposed_title: Layout (proposed by the reader, not confirmed)
checklist_templates.layout_explain: The reader proposed these from the workbook's structure — validation ranges, merged cells, runs of filled rows — never from its words. Check each column letter and each header cell against the grid, correct what is wrong, name the answer words, then confirm.
checklist_templates.header_explain: Each entry is a label cell the renderer leaves alone and a value cell it writes. Leave both empty when the template has no such entry.
checklist_templates.words_explain: The template's own words, whatever its language: which one means yes, which one no, and — only if this version offers it — which one means not applicable.
checklist_templates.words_none: The reader found no answer list it could read: type the template's words.
checklist_templates.word_na_hint: When the list has no such word, type one: the document will carry it, and the template's list is left as it is. A not applicable answer always needs its justification.
checklist_templates.confirm_clears_pairs: Confirming again reads the items anew and clears the pairs made by hand.
checklist_templates.evidence_explain: Say what proof a yes needs before a project's checklist can be submitted: none, a link or a file, or a file — and, for a proof that expires, for how many months it holds, 1 to 120; left empty, it does not expire. Only the lines you change are sent, on the revision on screen, and you become one of the draft's authors.
checklist_templates.evidence_kind_field: Proof asked by the item of row {{row}}
checklist_templates.evidence_months_field: Months a proof of the item of row {{row}} holds
checklist_templates.problem_evidence_months: A validity is a whole number of months from {{min}} to {{max}}, or left empty for a proof that does not expire.
checklist_templates.error_evidence: Could not set the proof the items ask for.
checklist_templates.refusal_not_draft: This version is no longer a draft: it is published or retired, and a published version never changes. To change it, derive a new draft from the published version.
checklist_templates.refusal_no_layout: This draft has no confirmed layout, so it has no items yet: confirm its layout first.
checklist_templates.refusal_changed: This version changed since you read it: you had revision {{revision}} on screen, and somebody else has edited, published or retired it since. Nothing was written over their change. Reload it, look at what changed, then try again.
checklist_templates.refusal_four_eyes_publish: You wrote this draft — you imported or derived it, confirmed its layout, paired its items or set what proof its lines ask for. Four-eyes approval is on, so a second person must publish it: another platform governor, administrator or CISO who did not write it. Written by: {{authors}}.
checklist_templates.refusal_four_eyes_retire: You wrote this version. Four-eyes approval is on, so a second person must retire it: another platform governor, administrator or CISO who did not write it. Written by: {{authors}}.
checklist_templates.refusal_retired: This version is already retired. Reload it to see where it stands.
checklist_templates.refusal_has_draft: This template already has a draft, and it has one at a time: publish that draft or set it aside before importing or deriving another version.
checklist_templates.refusal_not_published: A new draft is derived from a published version only, and this one is a draft or retired. Derive it from the template's published version instead.
checklist_templates.refusal_nothing_to_pair: This draft follows no published version, so there is nothing to pair its items with: every item is new.
checklist_templates.problem_sheet: Name the sheet the checklist is on.
checklist_templates.problem_required: Name the control, answer and comment columns: without them no item can be read nor an answer written.
checklist_templates.problem_letters: A column is named by its letters, from A to XFD.
checklist_templates.problem_rows: Name the first and the last item rows, the first at most the last.
checklist_templates.problem_header: A header entry names both cells — its label and its value, such as B3 — or neither.
checklist_templates.problem_words: Map the template's answer words to yes and no.
checklist_templates.problem_not_applicable: Name the word for not applicable, or stop offering it.
checklist_templates.pairing_none: No published version precedes this one: every item is new.
checklist_templates.pairing_explain: Each item against version {{ordinal}}: an unchanged item carries a project's answer as it is, a changed one carries it to be confirmed, an added one starts unanswered, a removed one's answer stays where it was given.
checklist_templates.pair_explain: Pair an added item with a removed one when they are the same control, reworded: the new item takes the old key, and a project's answer follows it, to be confirmed.
checklist_templates.publish_explain: Publishing makes this version what projects open their checklists on. A published version never changes: a new word, layout or binding is a new version, derived from it.
checklist_templates.publish_four_eyes: You wrote this draft, and four-eyes approval is on: it has to be published by a security lead (platform governor, administrator or CISO) who did not write it.
checklist_templates.publish_needs_layout: Confirm the layout before publishing: a draft without one has no items.
checklist_templates.confirm_publish: Publish revision {{revision}}, as shown on this page?
checklist_templates.confirm_set_aside: Set this draft aside? It will never be published.
checklist_templates.confirm_retire: Retire this version? No new checklist will open on it; those already on it stay readable.
checklist_templates.derive_explain: A derived draft keeps this version's workbook, layout and items, and is paired with this version.
checklist_templates.error_derive: Could not derive a new version.
checklist_templates.layout_confirmed_unpaired: Layout confirmed: {{count}} items read. The pairs made by hand were cleared — make them again if they still hold.
checklist_templates.derived_notice: Version {{ordinal}} derived as a draft from version {{from}}.
checklist_templates.retired_notice: Version {{ordinal}} retired: no new checklist opens on it.
checklist_templates.aria_undo_rule: Undo the rule change on row {{row}}
checklist_templates.rules_title: What each line is measured by
checklist_templates.rules_explain: A line bound to a rule is measured on every project from the evidence Vectispire recorded — scans, imports — and people still answer it: the measurement stands beside the answer. The binding is part of the line: a line whose rule moved is changed against the previous version. Keep a rule per line, then save: only the lines changed are sent.
checklist_templates.rules_read_only: The rule each line is measured by is bound on a draft whose layout is confirmed, by a security lead. A published version never changes: derive a new one to bind other rules.
checklist_templates.rule_kpi: KPI, as the template writes it
checklist_templates.rule_no_kpi: The template states no KPI for this line.
checklist_templates.rule_kpi_hint: The KPI stays text: no number is read out of it. Compare it with what the rule measures, below, before keeping the rule.
checklist_templates.rule_unbound_explain: No rule: people answer the line, and nothing is measured beside it.
checklist_templates.rule_incomplete: The rule is not complete yet: each of its parameters is stated, none is assumed.
checklist_templates.rule_field_max_age: Maximum age of the evidence, in days
checklist_templates.rule_max_age_hint: {{min}} to {{max}}. Older evidence is no data, never a pass. Seven days are proposed; nothing else is.
checklist_templates.rule_schedule_yes: Must run at least as often as the maximum age
checklist_templates.rule_scope_other: A plugin or an imported tool
checklist_templates.rule_scope_hint: A plugin by its id, an imported tool by its declared source's slug and the tool's name as the source declares it. The list suggests the plugins and the SARIF sources' tools that exist.
checklist_templates.rule_thresholds_optional: Optional: what the open vulnerabilities may hold. A severity left blank is not judged.
checklist_templates.rule_thresholds_required: At least one severity: at most so many open, at least such a share resolved (settled triage left out of both), or both. A severity left blank is not judged.
checklist_templates.rule_field_minimum_ratio: Minimum coverage, above 0 and up to 1
checklist_templates.rule_pattern_hint: The suite's whole name: * for any run of characters, ? for one — com.example.arch.*. Skipped tests do not count; a failed or errored one fails the line.
checklist_templates.rule_components_legend: Packages required, at the versions allowed
checklist_templates.rule_components_hint: An explicit list: a version is allowed when it is written here, as the SBOM states it. Nothing is ordered.

project_checklist.title: Security checklist
project_checklist.subtitle: The project's security checklist, answered line by line by the people who build it, then signed off by an approver.
project_checklist.not_found: This project does not exist or is not visible to you. A project's checklist is shown only to those who see the whole project.
project_checklist.error_write: The change could not be saved.
project_checklist.error_history: Could not load the line's history.
project_checklist.none: This project has no security checklist yet.
project_checklist.none_reader: This project has no security checklist yet. Somebody with write access opens one on a published template version.
project_checklist.no_offered: No template version is published yet: a security lead publishes one under Checklist templates.
project_checklist.open_explain: Choose the published template version this project answers. Every line starts unanswered.
project_checklist.four_eyes_applied: Applied: whoever signed it off wrote none of it.
project_checklist.four_eyes_not_applied: Not required when it was signed off.
project_checklist.four_eyes_on: On: whoever signs it off must have written none of this revision.
project_checklist.four_eyes_off: Off: one of its authors may sign it off.
project_checklist.read_only_old: An earlier revision, shown as it stands: it is never changed again.
project_checklist.read_only_role: You read this checklist; your role does not change it.
project_checklist.submit_blocked: Not ready to submit: lines {{lines}} still need attention.
project_checklist.sign_off_not_approver: Signing off is an approval: an administrator, a CISO or a security champion gives it.
project_checklist.sign_off_four_eyes: Four-eyes approval is on and you wrote part of this revision: a second person must sign it off.
project_checklist.field_return: Why is it returned? Its authors read the reason.
project_checklist.problem_reason: Say why the checklist is returned: its authors read the reason.
project_checklist.returned_notice: Revision {{revision}} returned to its authors, a draft again.
project_checklist.reopen_explain: The signed revision stays exactly as it was signed. A new draft opens on the same version, every answer and proof carried as current.
project_checklist.reopened_notice: Revision {{revision}} opened from the signed-off revision.
project_checklist.move_explain: Opens a new revision on the version chosen. On the same template each answer is carried: as current where the line is unchanged, awaiting confirmation where it changed; a new line starts unanswered. Another template carries nothing. The revision it leaves stays readable.
project_checklist.move_none: No other published version to move to.
project_checklist.takeover_hint: Answering replaces the automatic answer: the line becomes yours.
project_checklist.evidence_kind_link_or_file: A yes needs a link or a file as evidence
project_checklist.evidence_kind_file: A yes needs a file as evidence
project_checklist.awaiting_explain: This line changed since the answer was given. Answer it again, or confirm that the answer still holds.
project_checklist.comment_hint: Required for no and not applicable: whoever reads the checklist needs the reason.
project_checklist.problem_comment: A no or not applicable answer needs a comment saying why.
project_checklist.field_file: File, 25 MB at most — downloaded, never opened in the page
project_checklist.too_large: The request body is larger than the {{limit}} bytes this route accepts.
project_checklist.problem_link: A link proof is an https: or http: address.
project_checklist.problem_day: State the day the work was done: a day, and not in the future.
project_checklist.file_asked_hint: This line asks for a file: a link does not count as its evidence.
project_checklist.history_empty: Nothing written on this line in this revision.
project_checklist.conflict_changed: The checklist changed since you read it. Reload it, look at what changed, then try again.
project_checklist.conflict_line_changed: Somebody else wrote on this line since you read it. Reload the checklist to see their answer or evidence.
project_checklist.conflict_not_draft: This revision is no longer a draft: it was submitted, signed off or set aside meanwhile. Reload it.
project_checklist.conflict_not_submitted: This revision is no longer waiting for a sign-off. Reload it.
project_checklist.conflict_not_signed_off: Only a signed-off revision is reopened. Reload the checklist.
project_checklist.conflict_not_latest: A newer revision of this checklist exists: act on that one. Reload the checklist.
project_checklist.conflict_incomplete: Not every line is ready: lines {{lines}} still need attention.
project_checklist.conflict_incomplete_reload: Not every line is ready any more. Reload the checklist to see which.
project_checklist.conflict_four_eyes: Four-eyes approval: you wrote part of this revision, so a second person must sign it off. Written by: {{authors}}.
project_checklist.conflict_version_not_published: That version is no longer published. Reload to see the versions offered.
project_checklist.conflict_same_version: The checklist is already on that version. After a sign-off, reopen the signed revision to start again on it.
project_checklist.conflict_nothing_to_confirm: This line no longer has a carried answer awaiting confirmation. Reload the checklist.
project_checklist.conflict_evidence_withdrawn: That evidence was already withdrawn. Reload the checklist.
project_checklist.document_signed_hint: A zip of your template's workbook filled in and checklist.json, with their signatures: produced and signed at the sign-off, the same bytes at every download.
project_checklist.document_unsigned_hint: A zip of your template's workbook filled in and checklist.json, rendered now and not signed: its Evidence sheet opens with “Draft — not signed off”.
project_checklist.verify_intro: Check each signature against the platform's public key, obtained separately from the document —
project_checklist.verify_tlog: --insecure-ignore-tlog=true only says the signature was never published to Sigstore's public transparency log: Vectispire signs with its own key and publishes nothing. Without it cosign looks for an entry that does not exist. The key is what is checked.
project_checklist.aria_document_signed: Download the signed package of revision {{revision}}
project_checklist.aria_document_unsigned: Download an unsigned rendering of revision {{revision}}
project_checklist.document_not_found: The document of revision {{revision}} was not found: the project is no longer visible to you as a whole, or the revision does not exist. Reload the checklist.
project_checklist.conflict_measurement_contradicted: Line(s) {{lines}} are answered yes where the measurement is not met, and the submission is refused. Answer them as measured, or settle the findings through triage: a false positive leaves the figures once it is settled.
project_checklist.conflict_measurement_changed: A measurement changed since the submission — line(s) {{lines}}. A sign-off would attest to evidence that is no longer what was submitted: return the revision to its authors.
project_checklist.conflict_measurement_changed_answer: The measurement changed since you read it: it is read again here. Check what it says now, then answer.
project_checklist.sign_off_blocked_measured: Line(s) {{lines}} are measured otherwise than at the submission: the sign-off would be refused. Return the revision to its authors.
project_checklist.measurements_live: Measurements computed now ({{at}}) from the evidence recorded: live, never stored by reading them, and computed again at the submission and at the sign-off.
project_checklist.measurements_frozen: Measurements frozen by the sign-off: the evidence as it was judged then, not recomputed over data that has moved since.
project_checklist.measurements_stored: The measurements last stored for this revision, not recomputed.
project_checklist.answer_resting: This answer rests on the measurement read at {{at}}; the server applies the rule again and refuses it if the evidence moved.
project_checklist.answer_resting_dropped: Another answer than the measured one rests on no measurement.
project_checklist.reason_no_repository: The project has no repository: there is nothing to measure, and nothing passes by default.
project_checklist.reason_never_examined: A repository has never been examined for this: no scan or import in which the step looked. Not "nothing found" — nothing looked.
project_checklist.reason_step_absent: The step or plugin was absent in every scan within the maximum age: it did not look, which is not finding nothing.
project_checklist.reason_language_not_analysed: The analysis produced on a tree it could not read: a source language of the repository is read by none of the SAST rules the scan ran with, or the plugin reads none of the tree’s languages. Nothing found, because nothing was read.
project_checklist.reason_examination_unrecorded: The scans within the maximum age predate the record of which steps ran: whether it looked is unknown until the next scan.
project_checklist.reason_languages_unrecorded: The scan did not record the languages of its tree, or those its analysis reads: whether it read the code is unknown until the next scan.
project_checklist.reason_stale: The newest evidence is older than the rule’s maximum age.
project_checklist.reason_not_applicable_anywhere: The plugin applies to none of the project’s repositories: a line passed by a tool that looked at nothing would rest on absent data.
project_checklist.reason_suite_not_found: No suite of the newest test report matches the rule’s pattern.
project_checklist.reason_no_test_ran: The matching suites ran no test; skipped tests do not count.
project_checklist.reconciliation_contradicted: Contradicted: yes where the measurement is not met
project_checklist.reconciliation_understated: Understated: no where the measurement is met
project_checklist.measured_problem_contradicted: A yes against a measurement not met is refused at the submission
project_checklist.measured_problem_comment_required: No data: a yes needs a comment
project_checklist.measured_problem_evidence_required: No data: a yes needs a proof
project_checklist.measured_problem_evidence_expired: No data: the proof of this yes is out of date
project_checklist.measured_as_of: As of {{at}} — the oldest evidence it rests on
project_checklist.changed_since_submission: Changed since the submission, which found: {{outcome}}
project_checklist.no_data_answer_hint: No measurement to rest an answer on: answer it yourself. A yes where there is no data needs a comment and a proof.
project_checklist.as_measured_btn: Answer every measured line as measured
project_checklist.as_measured_hint: Each unanswered line measured met is answered yes, resting on the measurement shown; a line not met waits for your no and its comment.
project_checklist.as_measured_needs_comment: Lines {{lines}}, measured as not met, need your “no” with a comment:
project_checklist.as_measured_changed: The measurement of lines {{lines}} changed since you read it: check it again, then answer.
project_checklist.as_measured_not_shown: Lines {{lines}} are measured met now, which the page had not shown you: read them, then answer.
project_checklist.as_measured_no_data: Lines {{lines}} have no data: answer them yourself — a yes there needs a comment and a proof.
project_checklist.as_measured_already_answered: Lines {{lines}} were answered meanwhile: their answer is left as it is.
project_checklist.measurement_none: No measurement was stored for this revision.

checklist_rules.aggregation_project_weighted: over the project, weighted by size
checklist_rules.summary_schedule_required: Every repository's dependencies analysed by a scan that kept its SBOM, and the repository scheduled at least as often as the maximum age
checklist_rules.summary_schedule_not_required: Every repository's dependencies analysed by a scan that kept its SBOM; the schedule is not checked
checklist_rules.summary_scopes: Every scope looked on every repository: {{scopes}}
checklist_rules.summary_suite: Suites matching {{pattern}} ran at least {{tests}} tests, none failed nor errored
checklist_rules.problem_max_age: State the maximum age of the evidence: a whole number of days, {{min}} to {{max}}.
checklist_rules.problem_require_schedule: Say whether the repository's schedule must run at least as often as the maximum age.
checklist_rules.problem_scope_invalid: "{{scope}}" is no scope: builtin:<step>, plugin:<id> or import:<source>/<tool>.
checklist_rules.problem_threshold_needed: State a threshold for at least one severity — "no plaintext secret" is every count at zero.
checklist_rules.problem_max_open: {{severity}}: the most open issues is a whole number from 0 to {{max}}.
checklist_rules.problem_resolved_ratio: {{severity}}: the share resolved is a ratio from 0 to 1, four decimals at most — 0.6 for 60 %.
checklist_rules.problem_metric: Choose what the coverage counts: lines or branches.
checklist_rules.problem_minimum_ratio: State the minimum coverage: a ratio above 0 and up to 1, four decimals at most — 0.8 for 80 %.
checklist_rules.problem_aggregation: Choose whether every repository must meet it, or the project weighted by size.
checklist_rules.problem_pattern: Name the suites: a pattern of 1 to {{max}} characters, * for any run and ? for one.
checklist_rules.problem_minimum_tests: State the least number of tests the suites must run: a whole number, 1 to {{max}}.
checklist_rules.problem_purl: "{{prefix}}" is no package URL without its version: pkg:type/namespace/name, no space, no @, at most {{max}} characters.
checklist_rules.problem_versions: {{prefix}}: list 1 to {{max}} allowed versions, separated by commas.
checklist_rules.problem_version_length: {{prefix}}: an allowed version is at most {{max}} characters.
